allies.rationale_text: Signaling helps distinguish context-matched proof from mere prestige transfer by asking what adoption evidence actually communicates underlying quality.
allies.affinity_rationale: Signaling mechanisms underlie how social proof transmits behavioral information through observable choices
allies.activation_condition: When collective behavior communicates information through observable choices and actions

allies.rationale_text: Authority-bias amplifies social-proof contagion when endorsement from high-status members spreads faster than direct evaluation.
allies.source_quote: opinions from high-status members are especially contagious
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical lists Authority alongside Social Proof as part of the same group of influence principles that amplify when combined
allies.activation_condition: When influence from expert or authority figures amplifies conformity behavior

allies.rationale_text: Incentives clarify why copied behavior can drift from truth when actors are rewarded for prestige, affiliation, or conformity rather than causal accuracy.
allies.source_quote: context, incentives, or constraints do not match the current decision
allies.affinity_rationale: Incentive structures interact with social proof by aligning reward mechanisms with herd behavior patterns
allies.activation_condition: When reward structures align with or amplify herd behavior patterns

antagonists.rationale_text: Critical-thinking resists social-proof pressure by asking for evidence quality and disconfirming analysis instead of external affirmation.
antagonists.source_quote: Social Proof encourages accepting an idea based on external affirmation, which runs counter to the objectives of Critical Thinking.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical states social proof encourages accepting ideas based on external affirmation, which runs counter to critical thinking objectives
antagonists.activation_condition: When independent evidence evaluation is bypassed in favor of external social validation

antagonists.rationale_text: First-principles-thinking conflicts with social proof by stripping away inherited group assumptions instead of accepting collective behavior as a starting point.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical describes first principles as stripping away conventional means including social norms; social proof is built on accepting collective behavioral assumptions
antagonists.activation_condition: When collective behavioral assumptions prevent reasoning from foundational facts

structured_tensions.tension_text: Social-proof conflicts with critical-thinking when external affirmation is allowed to replace direct evidence review and disconfirming analysis.
structured_tensions.source_quote: Social Proof encourages accepting an idea based on external affirmation, which runs counter to the objectives of Critical Thinking.

curation_notes.summary: Layer 1+2 enrichment complete. authority-bias at 0.90 per canonical group of influence principles. first-principles-thinking antagonist elevated to 0.95 as canonical describes it as built on opposing assumptions.

open_questions: The source also supports cargo-cult pressure against causal analysis, but the kept set favors clearer current-vocabulary ids.
